meta.description: Designs QC, corrects signal drift, removes batch effects, filters features, normalizes samples, and imputes missing values for untargeted LC-MS/GC-MS metabolomics, framing each step as a measurement model that can create or erase biological signal.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOIs, PMIDs, p-values, or effect sizes across any of the 7 outputs; all references in SKILL.md are real, checkable citations.

practice_boundaries.detail: No diagnostic or prescriptive medical conclusions; this is a data-processing skill with no individual-subject claims.

methodological_ground.detail: Input 3: following SKILL.md's own documented one-line pattern (`impute.QRILC(feature_matrix_features_in_rows, tune.sigma = 1)[[1]]`) on raw (non-log) peak intensities -- the Skill's own stated input type, since its Pipeline Order table places imputation at step 5 and defers log/glog transformation to step 7 in a different Skill -- produced physically impossible NEGATIVE imputed intensities (e.g. -436.0, -159.5) with no error or warning. Verified by inspecting raw imputed values, not just summary stats. This is a principled methodological fallacy: fitting an unbounded truncated-normal model to non-negative, right-skewed MS intensity data.

code_usability.detail: All 7 inputs' generated R code executed without syntax errors or missing-dependency failures once minor implementation details (absolute paths, matrix-vs-SummarizedExperiment dispatch, sapply column names) were handled -- normal script-writing detail, not a defect in the Skill's own documented API calls.

functional_suitability.note: Exceptionally complete: four-operations table, pipeline-order rationale, two decision trees, quantitative thresholds with citations, per-method failure-mode table. Minor gap: doesn't document QCRSC's silent all-NA behavior below minQC (see input 4).

reliability.note: Common Errors table covers several real package quirks accurately (verified against pmp/statTarget). Gap: no warning that QCRSC and QRILC can both succeed with exit-code-0 while returning invalid/garbage output (inputs 3-4).

performance_context.note: 236-line SKILL.md, well-structured with tables; not bloated for the domain's genuine complexity.

agent_usability.note: Clear decision trees map directly to real function names and parameters; consistent terminology across sections.

human_usability.note: Strong discoverability via description and Quick-Start-style tables; Common Errors table gives good forgiveness.

security.note: No credential handling or destructive operations; strict-validation design is correct per the Data Analysis scene override.

maintainability.note: Well-modularized into SKILL.md + usage-guide.md + one runnable example; example script is self-contained base R so it doesn't drift with package versions.

agent_specific.note: Precise, detailed trigger description; explicit version-compatibility escape hatch ('introspect the installed package...'); strong composability via Related Skills links to xcms-preprocessing, statistical-analysis, batch-design.

inputs.note: executed: true. Demonstrated naive vs mod=-protected ComBat with an empirical false-positive-rate comparison across 54 true-null features. key_strengths: One of the most complete SKILL.md documents audited in this domain: four-orthogonal-operations table, pipeline-order rationale, two decision trees, a quantitative-thresholds table with real citations, and a per-method failure-mode table.

The canonical pipeline (detection filter -> QCRSC -> D-ratio/RSD filter) ran end-to-end on real MTBLS79 data with a genuinely non-circular held-out-QC validation, showing real RSD improvement (0.2298 -> 0.0780).

Correctly identifies and declines to 'fix' information-theoretically unwinnable batch/group confounds (input 5), recommending QC-anchored alignment over ComBat with the documented Nygaard 2016 caveat.
Common Errors table matches real package quirks verified independently against pmp/statTarget/imputeLCMD documentation.

recommendations.title: QRILC imputation on non-log intensities silently produces negative (impossible) values
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's documented one-line pattern `impute.QRILC(feature_matrix_features_in_rows, tune.sigma = 1)[[1]]`, run on raw peak intensities as the Skill's own Pipeline Order table specifies (impute at step 5, transform deferred to step 7 in a different Skill), produces negative imputed intensities with no error or warning.
recommendations.root_cause: impute.QRILC fits an unbounded truncated-normal model; it is designed for (and, in the proteomics literature it comes from, always used on) log-scale intensities, but the Skill's own pipeline places imputation before any log transform.
recommendations.fix: Add an explicit precondition to the Imputation section: log/glog-transform before calling impute.QRILC, then back-transform (2^x) the result; or reorder guidance so glog_transformation runs before MNAR imputation specifically.

recommendations.title: QCRSC silently returns all-NA features below minQC, with no error or warning
recommendations.problem: Calling QCRSC(minQC=5) with only 3 available QC injections in a batch does not error or warn; it returns every feature as entirely NA.
recommendations.root_cause: pmp's minQC guard operates per-feature/per-batch internally without surfacing a batch-level failure signal.
recommendations.fix: Add a row to the Common Errors table: 'QCRSC output is all-NA -> QC count below minQC for that batch; check colSums(!is.na(result)) == 0 immediately after every QCRSC call.'

recommendations.title: pqn_normalisation() has no documented way to retrieve the per-sample factor its own guardrail check needs
recommendations.problem: The Skill instructs checking whether the PQN normalization factor correlates with phenotype, but pqn_normalisation()'s return object exposes only dim/dimnames/processing_history/flags -- no factor attribute -- forcing a manual, undocumented recomputation.
recommendations.root_cause: The guardrail advice in the prose was written assuming an intermediate value the primary_tool's actual API does not expose.
recommendations.fix: Add a short code block showing how to recompute the per-sample quotient factor manually (reference median + row-wise median quotient) alongside the pqn_normalisation() call.

recommendations.title: Fixed r>0.3 phenotype-correlation guardrail is noise-sensitive at moderate sample sizes
recommendations.problem: At n=40 with dilution truly independent of group, the recomputed PQN factor still correlated with group at r=0.345, tripping the Skill's stated threshold from estimator noise alone.
recommendations.root_cause: No sample-size caveat is attached to the fixed 0.3 cutoff.
recommendations.fix: Note that the correlation check should use a permutation test or scale its threshold with n rather than a fixed r cutoff.

recommendations.title: ComBat-under-imbalance risk framing doesn't distinguish degree of confounding
recommendations.problem: At a realistic 85/15 batch/group imbalance (not perfect confounding), naive ComBat did not show the inflated false-positive rate the Skill's Nygaard-2016 caveat implies; the effect only appeared at perfect confounding (input 5).
recommendations.root_cause: The 'ComBat under imbalance' failure mode entry doesn't distinguish partial imbalance from near-total confounding.
recommendations.fix: Clarify that fabrication risk scales with the degree of batch/group association (e.g. report a chi-square/Cramer's V) rather than treating any imbalance as equally dangerous.
